title: HygieneNote Gingival Description and Intraoral Examination

source.exclusionReason: Chief Concern was already implemented before this specification.

cells.Normal Findings: Coral pink, with slight pigmentation in some ethnicities.
cells.Abnormal Findings: Red, bright red, bluish-red, pale pink, or white patches.
cells.Normal Clinical Notes: Gingiva appears coral pink with no erythema or discoloration.
cells.Abnormal Clinical Notes: Gingiva exhibits generalized redness in the anterior maxilla, indicative of inflammation. A localized bluish tint on the gingiva of #24–25 suggests cyanosis.

cells.Normal Findings: Knife-edged margins, flat against the teeth. Papillae fill embrasures.
cells.Abnormal Findings: Rounded, rolled, or bulbous margins; blunted, cratered, or enlarged papillae.
cells.Normal Clinical Notes: Gingival margins are knife-edged and flat against the teeth. Papillae completely fill the embrasures.
cells.Abnormal Clinical Notes: Gingival margins around #7–10 are rolled and rounded. Papillae between #8–9 are blunted.

cells.Abnormal Findings: Soft, spongy, or fibrotic; easily displaced with air or probing.
cells.Normal Clinical Notes: Gingiva is firm and resilient to palpation, with no areas of softness detected.
cells.Abnormal Clinical Notes: Gingiva is soft and spongy in the posterior sextants. Tissue compresses easily with air, and slight edema is present in the #18–19 region.

cells.Normal Findings: Stippled appearance on attached gingiva; smooth on marginal gingiva.
cells.Normal Clinical Notes: Attached gingiva displays appropriate stippling; marginal gingiva is smooth and intact.
cells.Abnormal Clinical Notes: Gingiva in the mandibular anterior region appears smooth and shiny with loss of stippling. A localized fibrotic texture is noted in the #2–3 area.

cells.Normal Findings: At or slightly below the CEJ, covering the root in younger patients.
cells.Normal Clinical Notes: Gingival margins are at or slightly below the CEJ with no recession or overgrowth noted.
cells.Abnormal Clinical Notes: Localized gingival recession of 3 mm is noted on #6–7 with root exposure. Generalized gingival overgrowth is present in the maxillary posterior region.

cells.Normal Findings: Pink, moist, no lesions or swelling
cells.Example Clinical Documentation: Buccal mucosa: Pink, moist, and intact bilaterally. Linea alba observed on the right side, consistent with the patient's occlusion history. No pathology detected.

cells.Normal Findings: Coral pink, firm, knife-edged margins, no bleeding
cells.Example Clinical Documentation: Gingiva: Generalized coral pink with localized redness in the posterior mandible. Bleeding noted upon probing in areas #30–31. Patient advised on oral hygiene improvements.
Tongue: Pink, moist, and symmetrical. Scalloping noted on the lateral borders, likely due to tongue thrust or parafunctional habits. Patient denies pain or discomfort.

cells.Normal Findings: Pink, smooth, no swelling or discoloration
cells.Example Clinical Documentation: Floor of mouth: Pink, smooth, and intact. Prominent veins observed bilaterally. No abnormalities noted.

cells.Normal Findings: Pink, intact, no lesions or abnormal growths
cells.Example Clinical Documentation: Palate: Torus palatinus observed on the midline of the hard palate. Mucosa pink and intact. No lesions or tenderness reported.

cells.Normal Findings: Uvula midline, no redness, swelling, or exudate
cells.Example Clinical Documentation: Oropharynx: Uvula midline. No swelling or exudate noted. Tonsils slightly enlarged but symmetrical. No complaints of pain or difficulty swallowing.
Teeth: Caries noted on #18 (MOD) and #30 (DO). Slight discoloration present on anterior teeth due to mild fluorosis. Patient educated on restorative treatment options.

cells.Abnormal Findings: Class II or III, open bite, crossbite, increased overjet/overbite
cells.Example Clinical Documentation: Occlusion: Class II Division 1 observed. Overjet measured at 5 mm. Patient advised on potential orthodontic options for correction if desired.
Saliva: Clear with adequate flow noted. Patient denies symptoms of dry mouth. Re-evaluate at the next visit for signs of potential xerostomia.

reviewItems.question: Should any CEJ/root-coverage wording from the source become a selectable normal finding?
reviewItems.currentDecision: No; preserve it only in raw source transcription until clinically reviewed.

reviewItems.question: Should fissured tongue remain abnormal or be treated as a normal variation?
reviewItems.currentDecision: Preserve the source classification but flag it for clinical review.

reviewItems.question: Should coated tongue always be classified as abnormal?
reviewItems.currentDecision: Preserve the source classification but flag it for clinical review.

reviewItems.question: Do Teeth, Occlusion, Saliva, Gingiva, or bleeding already exist elsewhere in the form?
reviewItems.currentDecision: Codex must inspect and reuse or summarize existing fields instead of creating competing state.
